result.title: The Role Of Recurrent Refinement In Medical Image Segmentation
result.summary: While feed-forward segmentation networks perform well on large cohorts, they degrade in constrained clinical settings with few training samples and imaging artifacts. Human vision, by contrast, remains robust under these conditions, a property partly attributed to the recurrent and feedback connectivity of the visual cortex, which refines visual information over time. Inspired by this, we append lightweight recurrent refinement blocks to segmentation backbones, namely Conditional Random Fields (CRFs), modern Hopfield networks and convolutional GRUs, and study their behaviour as the number of iterations increases at test time (including beyond the training horizon). Evaluated on two open-source datasets, Kvasir- SEG and ARCADE, our recurrent blocks add less than 1.5% parameters and yield gains on clean data (up to 1.4 pp) and under noise (up to 17 pp) while reducing HD95. Code is available at https://github.com/joaodsmarques/recurrencehelpsegmentation .

AI.brief_summary: 在分割骨干网络后附加 CRF、现代 Hopfield 网络和卷积 GRU 等轻量循环精修模块，并在 Kvasir-SEG 与 ARCADE 上考察测试时迭代次数增加（包括超出训练迭代范围）时的性能与稳健性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「循环精修 + 测试时迭代外推」可供核查 LVR 中迭代式 latent 状态更新、动态计算量与超出训练长度后泛化的关系，但任务是医学图像分割，缺少语言推理与多模态证据使用层面的验证。
